entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-8fmv-6rg5-5924: Kubeflow Pipelines: Pipeline archive upload allows decompression bomb to exhaust server memory
entry.content:
Kubeflow Pipelines: Pipeline archive upload allows decompression bomb to exhaust server memory

Aliases: CVE-2026-118761

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • github.com/kubeflow/pipelines — fixed in 0.0.0-20260831164314-ba9ae72cc860
  • github.com/kubeflow/pipelines

## Summary The Kubeflow Pipelines API server decompresses uploaded pipeline archives without adequately bounding expanded data in affected versions. A small ZIP or gzip-compressed tar archive can consume disproportionately large amounts of memory while the server locates or reads the pipeline file, potentially exhausting API-server resources and interrupting service. Multipart pipeline and pipeline-version upload processing decompresses the archive before namespace authorization, so a caller who can reach those endpoints does not need a successful pipeline-create authorization decision to trigger the issue. External authentication and network controls can restrict reachability. URL-import handlers authorize before fetching and decompressing a remote archive. The amount of expansion need…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-wg5q-x4j9-qm54: Kubeflow Pipelines: Run-log endpoint permits unauthorized access to pod logs
entry.content:
Kubeflow Pipelines: Run-log endpoint permits unauthorized access to pod logs

Aliases: CVE-2026-118759

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/kubeflow/pipelines — fixed in 0.0.0-20260904182349-be4723e33727
  • github.com/kubeflow/pipelines

## Summary The Kubeflow Pipelines API server's `GET /apis/v1alpha1/runs/{run_id}/nodes/{node_id}/log` handler retrieves logs without authorizing the caller against the selected run. A caller who can reach the backend and knows a victim run ID and a suitable pod or node identifier can read live or archived logs using the API server's permissions. For live logs, the vulnerable handler also accepts the supplied node ID as a pod name in the run's namespace without verifying that the pod belongs to the run. Depending on the API server's pod-log permissions, a known run ID can therefore permit reading the `main` container logs of an unrelated pod in that namespace. Logs may contain sensitive workload data or credentials. The affected handler does not authenticate the request itself. An extern…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-hff9-5pqw-6w9f: imgproxy has integer overflow in imgproxy ICO loader that causes denial of service and may permit remote code execution
entry.content:
imgproxy has integer overflow in imgproxy ICO loader that causes denial of service and may permit remote code execution

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • github.com/imgproxy/imgproxy/v3 — fixed in 4.0.16
  • github.com/imgproxy/imgproxy/v2 — fixed in 4.0.16
  • github.com/imgproxy/imgproxy — fixed in 4.0.16

## Summary The ICO loader allocates `data_size + BMP_FILE_HEADER_LEN` bytes after reading a 32-bit attacker-controlled `data_size`. For `data_size > UINT32_MAX - BMP_FILE_HEADER_LEN`, the addition wraps before allocation. imgproxy then writes the ICO prefix and reads up to the original declared size starting 14 bytes into the undersized allocation. A network client can turn this heap overflow into remote denial of service or remote code execution. ## Technical details The vulnerable path is in [`vips/icoload.c` at commit `f4fedbb`](https://github.com/imgproxy/imgproxy/blob/f4fedbb5c7f6684e7a8e0a9bb7e666773f3c40c0/vips/icoload.c#L154-L164): ```c uint32_t data_size = GUINT32_FROM_LE(largest_image_header.data_size); VipsPel *data = (VipsPel *) VIPS_MALLOC(NULL, data_size + BMP_FILE_HEADE…

imgproxy has unbounded memory allocation in ICO loader that allows unauthenticated memory-exhaustion DoS via crafted data_size field

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • github.com/imgproxy/imgproxy/v3 — fixed in 4.0.16

VipsPel *data = (VipsPel *) VIP…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-2wrx-84qj-4pcg: anacrolix torrent has unbounded recursion in the bencode decoder that causes stack-overflow crash and CPU-exhaustion DoS
entry.content:
anacrolix torrent has unbounded recursion in the bencode decoder that causes stack-overflow crash and CPU-exhaustion DoS

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • github.com/anacrolix/torrent — fixed in 1.61.1-0.20260911233437-76452a2c8a2f

## Summary anacrolix/torrent's bencode decoder (`bencode/`) applies **no limit on the nesting depth** of nested dictionaries and lists. Two distinct denial-of-service mechanisms follow from that single root cause, both reachable from a single crafted `.torrent` file or from metadata obtained from a peer on a magnet-link/v2 download: 1. **Stack-overflow process crash.** `Decoder.readOneValue` recurses once per nesting level with no depth bound. A `.torrent` whose `info` value is a list nested a few million levels deep (≈8 MB file) drives the recursion past the 1 GiB goroutine-stack limit and the process dies with an unrecoverable `fatal error: stack overflow`. 2. **Quadratic CPU exhaustion.** `metainfo.FileTree.UnmarshalBencode` (BitTorrent v2) re-parses each subtree at every level, makin…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-586p-749j-fhwp: Buildah allows arbitrary directory mount
entry.content:
Buildah allows arbitrary directory mount

Aliases: CVE-2024-9675, GO-2024-3186

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N · CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • github.com/containers/buildah — fixed in 1.38.0

A vulnerability was found in Buildah. Cache mounts do not properly validate that user-specified paths for the cache are within our cache directory, allowing a `RUN` instruction in a Container file to mount an arbitrary directory from the host (read/write) into the container as long as those files can be accessed by the user running Buildah.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-fgxm-5hvv-x4vh: charmbracelet/soft-serve HTTP responses disclose the existence and names of private repositories
entry.content:
charmbracelet/soft-serve HTTP responses disclose the existence and names of private repositories

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/charmbracelet/soft-serve — fixed in 0.12.3

## Summary Soft Serve answers Go's `?go-get=1` requests by walking up the requested path until it finds a repository, then rendering that repository's name and clone URL into a `go-import` meta tag. The walk checked that each candidate repository existed, but never that the caller could read it. A request for a path inside a private repository, such as `GET /secret/anything?go-get=1`, therefore returned `200` naming `secret` and its clone URL, even though `GET /secret?go-get=1` correctly returned `404`. The same `?go-get=1` exception in the HTTP access middleware also let requests reach the LFS and dumb-HTTP routes with the repository existence check skipped, where two LFS handlers dereferenced the missing repository and panicked. The same disclosure appears without `?go-get=1`. The Git…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-f3fj-9625-rv3m: charmbracelet/soft-serve: Race in `SetPrivate` leaves a private repository readable by unauthenticated users
entry.content:
charmbracelet/soft-serve: Race in `SetPrivate` leaves a private repository readable by unauthenticated users

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/charmbracelet/soft-serve — fixed in 0.12.3

## Summary Soft Serve cached repository records in memory with no expiry, and trusted the cached record for every access check. `SetPrivate` cleared the cached record before it saved the new visibility, and not afterwards. A request that arrived between the two read the old, public record from the database and cached it after the change was saved. From then on every access check used that stale record, so a repository the operator had just made private stayed readable by unauthenticated users over HTTP, SSH, and `git://` until the server restarted. ## Impact An unauthenticated attacker can keep reading a repository after it is made private, including everything pushed to it afterwards. The attacker needs no account and no timing knowledge: a client polling `GET /<repo>.git/info/refs?se…

## Summary `Challenge` resources under `acme.cert-manager.io` can be created directly by namespace users. On create, cert-manager performs no admission validation tying the Challenge to an `Order`, an owner reference, or an Issuer-selected solver. The ACME Challenge controller then reconciles the direct resource and uses `Challenge.spec.solver` as the DNS01 provider configuration. When the direct Challenge references a `ClusterIssuer`, cert-manager derives the DNS provider secret namespace and ambient-credential policy from the `ClusterIssuer` reference, but the DNS provider configuration itself is attacker-controlled through `Challenge.spec.solver`.
